questions.stem: A frame carries 100 bytes of data plus 25 bytes of headers and trailer. What percentage of the frame is data?
questions.explain: The frame is 125 bytes in all and the data share is 100 / 125 = 0.8, which is 80%.

questions.stem: A 1000-byte frame is sent on an 8 Mbps link (8 × 10⁶ bits per second). How many milliseconds does it take to push all the bits onto the link?
questions.explain: 1000 bytes is 8000 bits. 8000 / (8 × 10⁶) = 0.001 s, which is 1 ms.

questions.stem: A signal travels at 2 × 10⁸ m/s over a 2000 km link. How many milliseconds does it take to cross the link?
questions.explain: 2000 km is 2 × 10⁶ m. Time = distance / speed = 2 × 10⁶ / (2 × 10⁸) = 0.01 s, which is 10 ms.

questions.stem: In the TCP/IP and OSI models, which layer sits directly above the data link layer?
questions.explain: The order from the bottom is physical, data link, network, transport. IP lives in the network layer, just above the data link layer.
